sources.title: Haitians protest in support of El Salvador’s anti-gang troop deployment
Parlamento de Israel elege opositor de Netanyahu para comandar o Legislativo

en.title: Haitians protest support for El Salvador troops; Israel parliament elects opposition leader
en.dek: Protesters in Haiti back El Salvador's anti-gang deployment as Israel's parliament names Matan Kahana as its new president.
facts: Haitian demonstrators marched in support of El Salvador's anti-gang troop deployment despite concerns about instability.
El Salvador confirmed it would end its deployment of about 2,500 troops once four missing Salvadoran airmen were found.
Haitian Justice Minister Patrick Pelissier thanked Nayib Bukele for the troop surge and praised regained control of the national football stadium.
Israel's parliament voted to name Matan Kahana, a Yashar lawmaker and Gadi Eisenkot ally, as its new president with 66 votes.
Kahana's election followed the October general election that left Benjamin Netanyahu without a majority and triggered efforts to form a government.
body: Demonstrators have marched in several Haitian cities to show support for a deployment of troops from El Salvador, despite concerns that the outside intervention may worsen instability in the Caribbean country. On Tuesday, hundreds of protesters rallied in the streets of cities like the capital, Port-au-Prince, bearing signs with slogans like 'Down with the gangs'.

El Salvador confirmed it would end its deployment of about 2,500 troops once the missing Salvadoran airmen were found, but public gestures of support followed. Haitian Justice Minister Patrick Pelissier travelled to San Salvador and expressed gratitude for the troop surge, saying 'The Haitian people applaud the decision of Nayib Bukele to send troops.'

Matan Kahana, a parliamentary member of the Yashar faction led by Gadi Eisenkot, was named Israel's parliament speaker with 66 votes against 52 for another candidate. The current prime minister's faction condemned the vote, asserting that lawmakers had been elected with 'the votes of supporters of terrorism.'

Kahana rejected conditions tied to his election, writing that he was 'astounded' by the demand to ignore the Arab-Israeli public, which composes 21% of the general population. His election followed the October general election that removed Netanyahu's majority and left rival parties without a clear path to power.
en.context: Haiti has struggled with gang violence since the 2021 assassination of President Jovenel Moise, while Israel's parliament faced a political impasse after October general elections that ended Netanyahu's majority.
